The current conditions in Abuja indicate a temperature of 28°C, feeling more like 32°C due to the relatively high humidity of 67%. As we look ahead to the week, models suggest that a low-pressure system will begin to develop over the region, bringing with it an increased chance of rainfall. This system is expected to bring a mass of moist air from the southern coast, leading to increased humidity and precipitation. The Nnamdi Azikiwe Expressway, which is currently experiencing light traffic, may see some disruptions later in the week due to potential flooding in low-lying areas.

The rain chance is pegged at 45%, with the most likely time for precipitation being in the late afternoon and evening hours. The humidity will be on the rise, reaching a peak of 80% in the evening, making it feel quite muggy in the city. The low-pressure system will continue to strengthen on Monday, leading to an increase in cloud cover and precipitation. The low-lying flood-prone areas such as the Gwarinpa estate may experience some flooding, especially if the rainfall is more intense than expected.
